promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 5 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You hit every session on plan and the marathon-pace work landed right on target for sub-3:45. Next week steps the long run to 20 miles and keeps one quality session with marathon pace.

answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, please do not do that. Jumping from 40 to 80 miles in one week, 5 weeks out from the race, is a near-certain path to injury and would end your marathon before the start line. Your club mate did not get to 70 miles in one week either; they built there over months. You are already on a plan that will get you under 3:45 off your current volume. What wins a marathon in the last 5 weeks is the long run, one solid quality session a week, and arriving on Nov 1 healthy and rested. We will add a little volume where it helps, mostly on Sunday, and keep everything else honest.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

This week was the cleanest execution of the block, so we build on it instead of changing the shape. You followed every session, the Wednesday marathon-pace reps averaged 8:35/mi at heart rate 150, and the 15-miler finished with only +5.6 bpm of drift. That is a strong signal the current paces and volume are working.

Next week is the peak long run at 20 miles, kept easy. You already covered 20 under your own steam in the week of Sep 7, so the distance is familiar; this time we do it controlled, heart rate under 150, which is where the marathon-specific gain lives. The Wednesday session nudges from 6 to 7 miles at marathon pace to keep building confidence at goal effort without piling on new stress.

Volume lands near 47 miles, up modestly from 40. That is the right size of jump for this point in the build — big enough to matter, small enough to absorb. After this week we start trimming, with the week of Sep 28 being the last meaningful workout week before the taper opens.

On the 80-mile question: the honest coaching answer is in your answers above. Your fitness is on track. The thing most likely to lose you the race now is doing something your body has not been prepared for. Trust the long run as the key session and let the rest support it.
